item.title: Astros pick up Isaac Paredes’ $13.35 million club option for 2027
item.description: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images Astros pick up Isaac Paredes’ $13.35 million club option for 2027 appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Houston Astros have exercised a $13.35 million club option on infielder Isaac Paredes for the 2027 season, ensuring he remains under contract for another year following a productive 2026 campaign. The decision, which the team announced on Monday evening, comes as little surprise after Paredes made an emphatic statement with his bat in his first full season with Houston. The 27-year-old finished the year with a .262/.360/.447 batting line, an .806 OPS, 25 home runs, 27 doubles, one triple and 94 RBIs across 155 games. His RBI total tied for sixth in the American League. Paredes also demonstrated improved plate discipline, recording a 10.8% walk rate while striking out in just 13.4% of his plate appearances, the lowest mark of his career. Although his defensive performance at third base was considerably less convincing, yielding -7 Defensive Runs Saved and -4 Outs Above Average, he provided some additional flexibility by making short appearances at first and second base. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Paredes’ offensive influence reached its zenith at Daikin Park. He launched 14 home runs in 324 plate appearances at home, compared to 11 homers across 335 plate appearances on the road. The option exceeds his salary of $9.35 million in 2026 by $4 million. However, exercising it could save the Astros money, as Paredes was projected to receive approximately $15 million through arbitration had Houston declined the option. The 2027 campaign will be his final season of salary arbitration eligibility. The Astros’ decision also comes with potential roster implications. Houston enters the offseason with five established infielders competing for four positions: Paredes, Carlos Correa, Jeremy Peea, Jose Altuve and Christian Walker. Correa and Pena are healthy again after injuries disrupted their 2026 campaigns, while Yordan Alvarez occupies the designated hitter position. Consequently, the Astros could explore trade possibilities involving Paredes or Pena to address their crowded infield. Both players are also approaching free agency, with 2027 representing their final year of team control. For now, Paredes remains part of Houston’s plans, although his eventual position is uncertain. The Astros could also face a decision involving Walker, who is still owed approximately $20 million on his contract. One additional detail could affect Paredes’ contract. His club option could become a mutual option if he finishes among the top 10 in American League MVP voting. The award results are scheduled to be announced on November 12. item.title: Seton Hall basketball locks down Saint Peter's in season opener
item.description: NEWARK – Trey Parker took two dribbles to his right at the top of the arc, drew two defenders and slipped a perfect bounce pass to big man Devin Williams as he rolled off a screen. In one smooth motion, the 6-foot-10 Williams corralled the ball and sent it ahead from the foul line to the right corner, where Kareem Thomas stood unguarded. Thomas squared up and drilled a 3-pointer. The textbook offensive sequence, executed by three subs, was a promising glimpse during Seton Hall basketball’s 66-42 season-opening win against Saint Peter’s Monday: These Pirates are deep, balanced, and have the potential to be better offensively after a tough slog on that end the last two seasons. How many wins that will translate into over the next five months is anybody’s guess, but the efficient first-half stretch that included a 17-0 run was a welcome development after a meat-grinder exhibition win at Monmouth in the preseason. Saint Peter’s was picked to finish seventh out of 13 teams in the Metro Conference (formerly the MAAC) preseason poll after finishing second last season. The Peacocks returned their starting backcourt, including standout guard Bryce Eaton. This was the 93 rd meeting between these old neighborhood rivals, dating back to 1932. The Pirates lead 69-24. Starter Del Jones, a Radford transfer, struggled again after a tough outing at Monmouth, but his backups picked up the pace. Parker, who was sidelined during the exhibition after falling out of Shaheen Holloway’s good graces for undisclosed reasons, provided instant energy on the defensive end, disrupting Eaton and spearheading an effective full-court press. Parker, one of two returnees from last season, flourished in the press as a sophomore in 2025-26 and clearly maintains Holloway’s trust in that defense. And Illinois transfer Mihailo Petrovic did a fine job running the offense in relief of Jones, driving and dishing and finding the open man often enough to earn a low-five from Holloway as he checked out midway through the first half. 2. item.title: N.H. boys soccer: Zhe scores twice as Newmarket reaches Division IV final
item.description: NEWMARKET - Senior Brennan Zhe scored twice on free kicks, and that was all the top-seeded Newmarket High School boys soccer team needed in its Division IV semifinal against No. 4 Gorham. Zhe scored in the second minute and again in the 47th to lead the Mules to a 2-0 win Monday, Nov. 2 at Laconia High School. "Brennan could play in any position and be an all-state candidate," Newmarket head coach Kenny Najem said. "We have him at center back and he can neutralize attacks and turn them into counter attacking opportunities. He is the anchor of the defense and a leader of the whole team." Newmarket (17-0-2) will face No. 2 Littleton in Friday's Division IV championship game at Laconia High School. Littleton (15-1-3) advanced with a 2-1 semifinal win over No. 3 Epping. Newmarket and Littleton did not meet during the regular season. "Team is looking forward to the opportunity to play in the finals," Najem said. "We have a couple of practices to tighten some things up but at this point the boys just need to out show up and be ready to compete." Najem and the Mules watched the second half of Littleton's comeback win over Epping. "We saw some talented players tonight and we watched them show a lot of fight coming back from a 1-0 deficit to win 2-1," Najem said. This will be Newmarket's first trip to the state championship game since making consecutive appearances in 2018 and 2019. The Mules lost to Sunapee, 1-0, in the 2018 final before beating Sunapee, 2-0, for the 2019 championship. Newmarket has outscored its opponents 8-1 during this year's postseason, beating No. 16 Woodsville, 4-0, and No. 8 Moultonborough, 2-1, before shutting out Gorham. Newmarket goalie Matt Woods made seven saves in the semifinal. "(Woods) was excellent coming off his line for corner kicks and long throws," Najem said. item.title: Why Bellarmine coach Mo Reid thinks Louisville WBB can get to Final Four
item.description: Bellarmine women's basketball coach Mo Reid sported her Final Four ring in the Knights ' season opener at Louisville. She lived it in a Cardinals uniform, twice. Reid is the only player in UofL program history to make it to two of them. The Louisville native, now in her second season leading the Knights, had a courtside view of the current Louisville team setting a school scoring record in its 119-47 win over the Knights at the KFC Yum Center . Jeff Walz , now in his 20th season leading the Cards, has a team that is capable of reaching the Final Four. It's a place they're looking to get back to for their first time since 2018. Reid is confident her former school can get there. "This is the deepest team I've ever seen from him," Reid said. "And I even told him at at halfcourt after the game, 'I hope you win a national championship.' It makes me smile seeing it because I'm still prideful about my school. I mean, of course, I don't want them to whoop us like that. But I really wish Jeff all the best. And I really like the way, the direction of (where) this team is going." This UofL team has talent unlike anything the Bellarmine head coach has ever seen, but she pointed to the frontcourt in particular. "I've never seen a Louisville team like this, only because we've never had the bigs," Reid said. "They have the bigs, they have the size. We always had athletic tweeners." The head coach specifically noted LSU transfer Amiya Joyner, who finished with 14 points and five rebounds, as well as Virginia Tech transfer Carys Baker, who recorded 13 points, four assists and three rebounds. Both players came off the bench. "I was really impressed with the LSU transfer," Reid said of Joyner. "I think we've never had a traditional back-to-the-basket player since Chauntise Wright. She really impressed me. Of course, there's some things she has to work on or whatever, but I think she did a good job. And I think the Virginia Tech transfer (Baker), she really impressed me with how fast she shoots it at her size." Although Reid sported a maroon blazer at the Yum Center, it was hard to ignore the moments in the press conference where she referred to Louisville as "we." It's why she wore her ring when facing her former head coach. Reid still feels that sense of pride when speaking of the place where she cut down nets, and she has confidence that Louisville can get back to a place where she once was. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon State’s loss at Fresno State
item.description: FRESNO, Calif. — Oregon State lost to Fresno State 38-22 Saturday night at Valley Children’s Stadium. Here are 10 takeaways as the Beavers prepare to host Texas State. 1. Reality check Two things can be true. Oregon State can still be ahead of schedule and on its way to a legitimately surprising season amid a massive rebuild, complete with a potent offense. Much of its success thus far came by pounding less talented teams and several of the worst defenses in the country. And where OSU was vulnerable was there to be exploited by teams like Fresno State, which has talent and good coaching. The Beavers are not a College Football Playoff team. That dose of reality doesn’t diminish what’s being accomplished this season. They’re simply not one of the two most talented teams in the Pac-12 right now. 2. Oregon State was outcoached JaMarcus Shephard and his staff were outcoached for definitely the first time in conference play and arguably for the first time this season. Matt Entz laid out in detail what Fresno State picked up from studying Braden Atkinson from his time at Mercer and Oregon State’s tendencies. Bye weeks also include self-scouting. Fresno State was more prepared for what OSU showed and particularly offensively the Beavers did not have an effective counter. 3. Self-inflicted errors can’t happen in games like this Winning on the road against a team with at least comparable (if not better) talent and coaching is a difficult task to begin with. It becomes a whole lot harder with six presnap penalties and allowing five sacks with two leading to fumbles. OSU absolutely could have led by multiple scores early if not for a false start negating Jake Reichle’s would-be touchdown, if Aeryn Hampton’s foot was in bounds and if multiple other penalties didn’t occur. That doesn’t even get into defensive miscues from missed tackles or over-pursuits. 4. The offensive line may have had its worst game Houston was more physically dominating than Fresno State, but that’s to be expected. Oregon State’s offensive line had a brutal showing nearly across the board, with sacks allowed by multiple players in one-on-one matchups. OSU’s rushing stats are skewed by the sacks and not nearly as poor as the final box score, but the bottom line is Fresno State won the line of scrimmage and it’s not a particularly stout group. 5. item.title: Lightning star Nikita Kucherov says trade request stems from disrespect and lack of communication
item.description: TAMPA, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 5: Right wing Nikita Kucherov #86 of the Tampa Bay Lightning in the second period against the Philadelphia Flyers at Benchmark International Arena on October 5, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Parker S. Freedman/Getty Images) Getty Images TAMPA, Fla. (AP) — Reigning NHL MVP Nikita Kucherov requested a trade from the Tampa Bay Lightning because he feels disrespected by a lack of communication with general manager Julien BriseBois. “It was never about the money for me,” Kucherov told reporters after practice on Monday. “More about poor communication and respect. Over the last four months, we only have had two conversations and Julien, in the end, made it clear that I’m free to walk on July 1.” Kucherov will become an unrestricted free agent on that date. He’s in the final season of an eight-year, $76 million contract signed in 2018 before he helped Tampa Bay win the Stanley Cup twice, led the NHL in scoring three times and won the Hart Trophy in 2018-19 and 2025-26. Asked what the organization has meant to him, Kucherov said: “Everything. Got drafted here, played for, now this is my 14th year. A couple championships, met a lot of great people. You know, everything. My kids grew up here, and I’m forever grateful for this organization.” Kucherov’s 1,142 points in 892 regular-season games since debuting in 2013 are third most among all players over that time behind only Edmonton’s Connor McDavid and Colorado’s Nathan MacKinnon. His 177 points in the playoffs are the most during that span. The 33-year-old Russian winger became the franchise’s career points leader last month, passing former captain Steven Stamkos. Kucherov has four goals and 14 assists for a team-leading 18 points through 13 games. The Lightning are 7-3-2. They’ve been eliminated in the first round of the playoffs four consecutive years after falling two wins shy of a three-peat in 2022. “We unequivocally have no intention of trading Nikita,” BriseBois said in a statement last week. BriseBois told reporters in mid-September that the goal was to get Kucherov signed to a new deal that keeps him around for years to come as part of a perennial contender. BriseBois said he and agent Dan Milstein would keep the lines of communication open to that end. “For now, I’m part of this team, and I’ll do anything I can to help my teammates win,” Kucherov said. He added that he personally informed his teammates of his trade request. “They heard it from me first. Those guys are my family and this will never change,” he said.

item.title: Detroit Red Wings get sunny start to Florida trip with win vs Panthers
item.description: SUNRISE, FL – Daniil Tarasov returned to face his old teammates and Carter Mazur celebrated his first career NHL goal. The Detroit Red Wings played the first of a quick – very quick – trip to the Sunshine State (though it was more of a stormy state outside Ameran Bank Arena on Monday, Nov. 2), opening with a visit to the Florida Panthers. Looking for a bounce-back after a blown opportunity at home, the Wings responded by banking two points over an Atlantic Division rival with a 5-3 victory. Tarasov, a former Panther, made 23 saves. Justin Faulk and Michael Brandsegg-Nygard scored 45 seconds apart before the third period was three minutes old to give the Wings some breathing room. Faulk ripped a slapshot during a power play, taking advantage of Michael Rasmussen's screen, at 2:06, and at 2:53, Brandsegg-Nygard finished a nice feed from the corner from Lucas Raymond. Sam Bennett cut it to a one-goal game with 3:20 to play, and the Panthers pulled their goalie for an extra attacker. But Emmitt Finnie scored an empty-net goal with 2.7 seconds on the clock. Leonard played on the third line, with J.T. Compher and Rasmussen. item.description: ‘They’re Going To Want Mike Tomlin’ — Ex-NFL QB Speculates on Cowboys Pursuing Legendary HC While Raising Doubts About Dak Prescott After dropping their third game in the past four matchups, the losses are starting to pile up for the 3-5 Dallas Cowboys. With team owner Jerry Jones always setting playoff expectations, head coach Brian Schottenheimer’s seat may be warming up. Yet, if the Cowboys do move on from coach Schottenheimer, who would take over? Some are already pointing to Mike Tomlin, who’s now acting as an NFL analyst with NBC Sports. Meanwhile, others are questioning how long the team will stick by franchise quarterback Dak Prescott, who’s only under contract through 2028. Add it all up, and there could be some sizable changes coming to the Cowboys before the 2027 season kicks off. Dallas Cowboys Ready to Ditch Dak Prescott and Hire Mike Tomlin? The Cowboys have shown they’re not afraid to mix things up when things get stagnant. Yet, Prescott is now in his 11th season as the Cowboys’ starting quarterback. However, after leading the team to just a 2-5 record in the postseason, some feel like the Cowboys could do better than what the four-time Pro Bowler has offered. In fact, former NFL quarterback Chris Simms suggested during Monday’s edition of “ PFT Live ” that Prescott’s days in Dallas could be numbered. Perhaps just as interesting was Simms offering Tomlin as an eventual replacement for coach Schottenheimer, too. “They’re going to want Mike Tomlin,” Simms said. “The future of Dak, for what they’re paying Dak. Dak is not one of the top quarterbacks in football. That’s not even debatable. Of course, he’s got some of the best support around him. You could get in this convo of where Dak stacks up. item.description: ‘We Gonna Get You out of There’ — Legendary NFL WR Puts Cowboys on Notice Over George Pickens’ Lack of Opportunities in Dallas George Pickens had another quiet game in the Dallas Cowboys’ Week 8 overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals at AT&T Stadium. He caught just two of four targets for 48 yards, and through eight games so far, he has recorded only one 100-yard performance. Pickens’ lack of involvement is becoming harder to ignore, especially with Dak Prescott and the Cowboys’ offense continuing to lean heavily on other targets. After Sunday’s loss, NFL legend Chad Johnson questioned why Dallas wasn’t getting the ball into Pickens’ hands more often and even suggested the receiver could be better off elsewhere. Chad Johnson Calls Out Cowboys Over George Pickens’ Lack of Targets During Monday’s episode of the “Nightcap” podcast, Johnson came to Pickens’ defense and took aim at how the Cowboys have used him this season. “Get him the ball, man. He had 2 of 4 today. What are we doing? Y’all were begging for NFL Youngboy to stay in Dallas doing all this hooping and hollering… Cursed me out, ‘Oh, you hating on the Cowboys. Let Pickens stay here. We want him here.’ And look at what y’all are doing to him,” Johnson said . When co-host Joe Johnson asked whether Prescott should force-feed Pickens, the former NFL wideout didn’t hesitate. “Yes, force-feed him. They ain’t got a problem throwing CeeDee [Lamb] 157 balls in one game… He had four targets in a four-quarter game,” Johnson continued. When his co-hosts suggested Pickens wasn’t giving full effort, Johnson pushed back hard. “Loafing my [expletive]. Let him go. If he was loafing, you shouldn’t have wanted him there then. Hey, Pick, hold your head up, boy. You good. Just stay locked in. Me and [David] Mulugheta, we’re gonna get you out of there.” David Mulugheta has represented Pickens since he entered the NFL Draft process in 2022. Through eight games this season, meanwhile, CeeDee Lamb has been targeted 92 times, catching 60 passes, compared with George Pickens’ 62 targets and 39 receptions. Lamb has the edge in receiving yards and touchdowns, with 709 yards and six scores to Pickens’ 533 yards and two touchdowns. However, Pickens leads in yards per reception, averaging 13.7 to Lamb’s 11.8. item.description: Mandatory Credit: Joe Camporeale-Imagn Images. Credit: USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Connect | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Marilee Gallagher, Manager We finally have more information about the John Cena Classic from the man himself. On Monday, John Cena returned to Monday Night Raw for the first time since his retirement tour wrapped up in December 2025. In his return, Cena said he was there in Brooklyn because if you have a big announcement to make, you do it in the Big Apple. And Cena had not one, not two, but three announcements as it relates to the upcoming John Cena Classic. Everything We Know about the John Cena Classic The JCC is Going to Disney World on a Night that Will Make History Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect On December 14, WWE will air two episodes of Monday Night Raw on the same day for the first time in history. The earlier Raw will air in the afternoon, live from Perth, Australia , while a special edition will air at Raw’s normal start time, featuring matches exclusively part of the John Cena Classic. That episode of Raw will take place at the ESPN Wide World of Sports Complex in Disney World in Orlando, Florida. It will be the first time WWE will air an episode of Raw from that location. In September, TKO CEO and President Mark Shapiro addressed speculation that WWE was looking to potentially run events from the ESPN Florida complex , stating, “Frankly, I’m excited about 2027 as we’re working with the Walt Disney Company on some special events around Disney and WWE and bringing those two audiences together since, of course, what do they have in common? Family.” According to the report, WWE’s talks with Disney actually predated the company’s talks and later partnership with ESPN. The Voting Lives in Club WWE Cena’s second piece of news was that the voting aspect of the JCC, the most discussed and questioned element ever since Cena first announced the tournament’s existence, will live entirely within Club WWE. This should come as little surprise to people, given Cena’s involvement in Club WWE’s launch . He has been the face of the new fan-focused subscription service. Club WWE requires membership, which means the voting aspect of this event will be limited to subscribers. It seems unfortunate to put the voting for this behind a $99 paywall, but WWE is all about the bottom line. Being able to vote in the John Cena Classic will almost certainly increase the subscriber count for the new service. It seems like WWE might be banking on that ploy in much the same way streaming services release new shows to garner additional interest. item.title: Kenny Dillingham addresses coaching rumors, says Jake Fette is starter
item.description: It’s that time of year again — Arizona State coach Kenny Dillingham is being connected to coaching rumors. This time, it’s a place he knows well: Tallahassee. With Florida State firing Mike Norvell on Nov. 1, the coaching carousel is starting to fly again, and Dillingham is firmly planted on it. It’s not the first time. It was Michigan in 2025 , which directly led to a lucrative contract extension for Dillingham . When asked about the Florida State opening, Dillingham addressed it, but did not directly squash it. “We’ve done this before,” Dillingham said with a smile and slight chuckle at his weekly Monday press conference on Nov. 2. “I’m trying to find a way to beat Colorado," he said. "This is a team that people don’t talk about enough, in my opinion. They’ve been in every single football game. They’ve had leads in almost every single football game. They stop the run at a high rate. They’re explosive on offense. This is a good football team. I’m 100% of the mindset: ‘Let’s go play our best football game versus Colorado.” Later, when asked about the possibility of a reunion with Norvell — who gave a young Dillingham his first opportunity in college football — in Tempe, Dillingham indicated he did not see that happening. “Probably not going to happen," Dillingham said. "He’s not going to come back here. He’s going to have a lot of opportunities to go be a head coach somewhere. I’m rooting for him.” — Logan Stanley Fette likely to remain starter After getting his first start against BYU, it looks like freshman quarterback Jake Fette is going to remain the starter for the Sun Devils moving forward. When asked who the starting quarterback is, Dillingham gave a straightforward answer. “I think right now you gotta say it’s Jake Fette,” Dillingham said. “I think he’s earned it. Mikey’s (Keene) working his way back. But I think Jake played really, really well in the second half, especially for a freshman on the road in that environment. To really take command, the way he played in the second half, was of a veteran. That gave me a lot of hope.” Dillingham liked how Fette communicated on the sideline by quickly and accurately identifying his mistakes and taking ownership. Fette struggled in the first half against BYU under heavy pressure, completing 9-of-18 passes for 47 yards while being sacked six times. The second half was much improved for Fette, going 7-of-14 for 61 yards and two touchdowns. Notably, Fette was sacked zero times in the second half. “Even with how he just managed the football game was confident,” Dillingham said. “There was one time I had to burn a timeout. But other than that, procedurally he was clean. He motioned. He made checks. He was aware of the clock. item.title: Third-period flurry fuels Red Wings in 5-3 victory over Panthers
item.description: SUNRISE, Fla. — A startling flurry did the Red Wings in the other day, but not this time. Goals from Justin Faulk (power play) and Michael Brandsegg-Nygard 45 seconds apart early in the third period Monday, Nov. 2, sent the Wings to a 5-3 victory over Florida. BOX SCORE: Red Wings 5, Panthers 3 The Wings allowed three quick goals midway in the third period Saturday, Oct. 31, to St. Louis in a what turned out to be a disappointing and shocking loss . But this time it was the Wings who astoundingly turned the game around. Faulk's power-play goal, a one-timer at 2 minutes 8 seconds, gave the Wings a 3-2 lead. Andrew Copp teed up Faulk in the high slot and Faulk fired his third goal of the season past goaltender Jacob Markstrom. Brandsegg-Nygard scored his third goal, at 2:53. Brandsegg-Nygard got free in front and Lucas Raymond found him alone, Brandsegg-Nygard poking the puck past Markstrom. Florida's Sam Bennett cut the lead to 4-3, with Markstrom pulled for an extra attacker, at 16:40. But Emmitt Finnie's empty net goal with 2.7 seconds left clinched the Wings' victory. The Wings (7-5-3) have won six of their last nine games (6-2-1), with a game Tuesday, Nov. 3 in Tampa to conclude a quick, two-game road trip. Florida's Aaron Ekblad scored a shorthanded goal, tying the game at 2 at 15:25 of the second period. After Markstrom made a good save on one end, the Panthers rushed the puck up ice, and Eklbad put back a rebound off goaltender Daniil Tarasov's skate and into the net for his first goal this season. Alex DeBrincat gave the Wings a 2-1 lead early in the second period. A Panthers defender fell, creating a 3-on-1 rush for the Wings. Viktor Arvidsson found DeBrincat on the opposite wing, and DeBrincat buried a shot for his seventh goal, at 1:26. Carter Mazur and Florida's Sam Reinhart traded first-period goals. For Mazur, it was his first NHL goal in 18 career games. Mazur came off the ice and gathered the puck after Moritz Seider's hard rim around the boards. Mazur skated to near the dot and lifted a shot that beat Markstrom at 5:26. But Reinhart got the Panthers even late in the first period. The Panthers won a battle along the boards, Carter Verhaeghe got the puck, and found Reinhart who skated into the slot and beat Tarasov for his eighth goal, at 14:19. tkulfan@detroitnews.com @tkulfan This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Third-period flurry fuels Red Wings in 5-3 victory over Panthers

item.title: Mallory Heyer impresses in Oregon women's debut vs. Hawaii
item.description: It didn't take long for Mallory Heyer to make a splash, or several, in Oregon women's basketball's 87-54 win over Hawaii on Nov. 2 at Matthew Knight Arena. The fifth-year transfer from Minnesota arrived in Eugene halfway through the season last year, but sat it out while practicing with the team . In the Ducks' (1-0) season opener Monday afternoon, Heyer scored 16 points in the first half and showcased disciplined versatility in the dominant win. "We expect that from Mallory," coach Kelly Graves said. "She’s been shooting the heck out of it pretty, much all fall." Heyer didn't score in the second half but continued to impact the game on the boards and defensively, totaling seven rebounds, a steal and a block in her Duck debut. At 6-foot-1, Heyer is undersized for a forward and plays alongside a fellow undersized forward in 6-foot Ehis Etute. The junior Etute contributed 15 points and 14 rebounds after a slow start in a promising opener for Oregon's frontcourt. "We’re working on spacing the floor and hitting outside shots and opening up the inside, eventually, too," Heyer said. "Just doing whatever the defense gives us." Heyer will continue to be a big factor in Oregon's offense moving forward, Graves said, as she looks to slot into a role occupied by Mia Jacobs a year ago as a pick-and-pop rebounder. "She’s one of our better 3-point shooters," Graves said of Heyer. "She kind of cooled off a little bit, but she’s able to stretch the defense … when teams have to stay on Avary Cain and stay on Mallory, that gives Katie (Fiso) a lot of room to operate with the ball and gives Ehis some freedom to make plays inside." Oregon happy with 3-point shot selection in debut win Graves mentioned after Oregon's exhibition win against Bushnell the Ducks are aiming to get off around 30 3-point shot attempts per game. The Ducks hit that number and then some in a back-and-forth and fast-paced game. At one point the Ducks were well on pace for more than 40 3-point shot attempts and knocking them down at a decent clip. The well eventually dried up, especially in the second half, and the Ducks finished 11 for 32 on 3-point attempts. Oregon eclipsed 30 3-pointers in a game just four times and averaged 19.4 per game a year ago. In the Graves era, Oregon's single-season high for 3-point attempts per game is 23.8. "I thought we got a little stagnant offensively," Graves said. "We’re at our best when we’re moving the ball, but I think we had some players dribbling a little bit too much, always calling for ball screens. "I liked our shots. I think a lot of those are going to fall in the future if we continue to get those shots." Katie Fiso, who scored 14 points and dished out nine assists, mostly to shooters, said while she doesn't have a number in her head for how many Oregon should take a game, her focus is on making the "right read." item.title: Undefeated East Hampton girls soccer wins Shoreline Conference championship, first in two decades
item.description: The East Hampton girls soccer team won the Shoreline Conference championship 1-0 over Old Saybrook at Blythe Field in Deep River Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. (Joe Morelli / Hearst Connecticut Media) DEEP RIVER - Ten starters returned for the East Hampton girls soccer team this season. Last year's team won 17 games, a successful season by any measurement. But there were no postseason championships to show for it. The Bellringers reached last year's Shoreline Championship final, but suffered their first defeat of the season to Valley Regional . East Hampton was back in the Shoreline final again Monday night, again having gone unbeaten. This time was different: top seed East Hampton defeated No. 3 Old Saybrook 1-0 at Blythe Field. "We were really motivated this year to come back," East Hampton junior Olivia Correia said. "We were, like, hungry for it, we really wanted it, and we knew that no one was going to give it to us, so we had to come out and work really hard." This was East Hampton's first Shoreline title since 2006, the Bellringers' first season in the Shoreline after leaving the Charter Oak Conference. Correia, the Shoreline Player of the Year, assisted on the first-half goal for East Hampton (17-0-0) with 5:50 left before halftime. Correia dribbled through several defenders and found fellow Junior Ava Ploszay, who scored past Old Saybrook goalkeeper Amarra Holmes. "I saw Ava run like off her mark and I just played the ball through the defenders and she tapped it in," Correia said. Said Ploszay: "I saw Liv dribbling up the middle going by people. I saw my mark turn her head. I knew I had the opening, so I was just running. Liv played the through ball. … Before I knew it, I tapped in the goal." East Hampton, the No. 1 team in the Class M/S state coaches poll, won all five of its one-goal games it has played this season, including against Old Saybrook 1-0 in the season opener. East Hampton will be the top seed in the CIAC Class M state tournament and receive a first-round bye. "We have worked all season long, probably two seasons long, to get to this point, to get back to this point, and prove a point that our regular season record wasn't a fluke and that we really wanted to take it home this year, especially after last year losing in the final," East Hampton girls soccer coach Andrea Giuliano said. This was Old Saybrook's third Shoreline Conference tournament final this decade. The Rams (13-3-3) have had a fine season as well and will likely be the No. 3 seed in Class S when the CIAC pairings are announced on Tuesday. Old Saybrook had no shot attempts in the first half. But the Rams were able to get five shots off in the second half. One in particular, East Hampton goalkeeper Cassie Owocki had to make a diving save for. Owocki's counterpart, Amarra Holmes, made eight saves. Her effort kept it a one-goal game in the second half.
